conventions.vorticity: W_ij=epsilon_ijk omega_k; W x=−omega cross x

claims.title: Two nonparallel source derivative directions complete the jet
claims.statement: Known J(x)=h∇_x U and optical D yield residuals y=−W x=omega cross x. Two nonparallel source-spatial directions give G=sum w(I−xxT)>0 and omega=G^−1 sum w x cross y.
claims.proof: Triple product identity and positive normal matrix.
extra_information: Independent local source derivative measurements or their covariant limiting contract
Known source identification, length and spacetime transport
Independent optical u,B
limits: No equivalence to observer-time proper motion is asserted.
A static remote sky does not supply these derivatives.
claims.novelty: Standard geometric/finite-dimensional ingredients assembled into an explicit sufficient information theorem; no priority claim.

extra_information: Input and transport error bounds
Operator lower singular value

claims.title: Radiation residual reconstructs the three vorticity components
claims.statement: Independently supplied horizontal spacetime brightness derivative and collision moment form r=(W e)·grad_S I. Its second moment is R=[M,W], invertible on so(3) when M has three distinct eigenvalues. Weak form requires brightness moments only through rank four.
claims.proof: Geodesic direction and energy equations, energy integration by parts, zero divergence of rotational sphere field, angular integration by parts.
extra_information: Radiation brightness in known source frame
Independent covariant spacetime derivative moment T2
Specified and bounded collision moment C2
Known physical frame transport
Optical A,theta,sigma
limits: Do not calculate T2 through trial-W transport then reuse it as evidence.
Scalar first-jet optical data alone do not supply T2.

claims.title: Radiative residual finite-error inverse
claims.statement: Exact M gap delta gives ||delta W||F<=epsilon_R/delta. With M uncertainty epsilon_M and ||W||F<=W*, bound is (epsilon_R+2 epsilon_M W*)/deltahat.
claims.proof: Singular values of commutator on so(3) and ||[delta M,W]||F<=2||delta M||op||W||F.
extra_information: Residual errors inclusive of collision, frame, spectral and optical-rate errors
Nonzero calibrated commutator response gap
limits: Gap can fail for symmetric radiation states.
No amplitude-independent bound for arbitrary operator error.

claims.title: Stacked degenerate quadrupoles can jointly reconstruct W
claims.statement: W -> ([M_j,W]) is injective iff intersection of antisymmetric commuting subspaces is zero. Its Gram lower eigenvalue supplies the inverse bound. Two nonisotropic axisymmetric M_j with nonparallel axes suffice.
claims.proof: Normal matrix positivity; axisymmetric commutator implies omega parallel symmetry axis; intersection vanishes.
extra_information: Independently known residual for every channel
Common physical frame
Band boundary fluxes for spectral channel residuals
limits: Additional moment tensors without their independent residuals are not enough.
claims.novelty: Standard geometric/finite-dimensional ingredients assembled into an explicit sufficient information theorem; no priority claim.

claims.title: Bounded collision map and exact conditional angular quadrature
claims.statement: Restricted rest-electron Thomson integral has L2 Frobenius norm <=(5/2)Gamma. With scalar bandlimits L,LC,LT, quadrature degree D*=max(L+4,LC+2,LT+2) suffices using Nmu>=ceil((D*+1)/2), Nphi>=D*+1.
claims.proof: Projection contraction and Cauchy–Schwarz; Fourier cancellation and Gauss–Legendre polynomial degree.
extra_information: Full coherent radiation state when polarization gain matters
Thomson regime, electron frame and density
Exact bandlimits or tail/error bounds
limits: Conservation alone does not identify collision source.
Finite state round-trip exactness does not imply product exactness.
No spin quadrature generalization is assumed.
claims.novelty: Standard geometric/finite-dimensional ingredients assembled into an explicit sufficient information theorem; no priority claim.

claims.title: Type-free conditional tilt closure
claims.statement: Independently supplied spacelike homogeneous-orbit generators with positive Gram matrix define future N by normalized dual wedge; gamma=−u.N and beta²=1−gamma^−2 give relative tilt.
claims.proof: Dual wedge orthogonality and squared norm=−det Gram.
extra_information: Actual orbit tangent distribution, independently identified
Recovered source field u on requested domain
limits: Does not identify generators from optical data.
One event establishes only one-event tilt.
